question: Rudrasena II of which of the following dynasties married Prabhavatigupta, the daughter of Chandragupta II of the Gupta dynasty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vakataka**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Prabhavati Gupta married Rudrasena II of the Vakataka dynasty: 
 
• Prabhavati Gupta
 
 
• The daughter of Chandragupta II, the ruler of the Gupta Empire, and queen Kuberanaga.
 
• She was a powerful monarch in early Indian history. 
 
 
 
• Rudrasena II
 
 
• The ruler of the Pravarapura-Nandivardhana branch of the Vakataka dynasty.
 
• He ruled in the Deccan region to the south of the Gupta empire. 
 
• Rudrasena II's reign was short, from around 385–390 CE.
 
• He died early, leaving his sons Divakarasena, Damodarasena, and Pravarasena II minors.
 
 
 
• Prabhavati Gupta ruled as regent for an extended period of time. 
 
• Rudrasena became a devotee of Chakrapani or Vishnu, unlike his ancestors who were all devout Shaivites.
 
• His change of faith was probably encouraged by his father-in-law and his queen, who were both staunch Vaishnavites. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pushyabhuti
 
 
• Also known as the Vardhana dynasty, this dynasty ruled in northern India during the 6th and 7th centuries.
 
• The dynasty's last ruler, Harsha Vardhana, ruled from Kanyakubja (modern-day Kannauj, Uttar Pradesh) and extended his empire to Kamarupa in the east and Narmada River in the south. 
 
 
 
• Chalukya
 
 
• This dynasty ruled in central and southern India, consolidating its power after defeating the Pallavas and the Gangas.
 
• The Chalukyas expanded their power over the Deccan Plateau after Pulakesin I. 
 
 
 
• Pallava
 
 
• This dynasty ruled in northern Tamil Nadu and was a major power for a brief time.
 
• The Pallavas' art and architecture include the Vaikuntha Perumal Temple at Kanchipuram, the Shore Temple, and the Pancha Rathas of Mahabalipuram
